speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your urgency, but identifying the specific cause is critical. Given the "painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions," could you tell me if you have a known history of HIV infection or a recent tick bite? REQUEST TEST: HIV_Serology REQUEST TEST: Titer_for_Rickettsia

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HIV_Serology: Negative; Titer_for_Rickettsia: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rickettsialpox (or similar rickettsial disease) despite negative initial serology, possibly early presentation; however, the clinical picture of painful monoarticular wrist arthritis with violaceous vesiculopustular lesions strongly suggests a specific diagnosis of **Cat Scratch Disease (Bartonella henselae) presenting with regional lymphadenopathy mimicking arthritis and characteristic skin lesions**. Given the negative Rickettsia titer and HIV status, and the specific description of "painful" wrist (not just tender) with erythema and swelling, this is likely **Bartonellosis**. 

REQUEST IMAGES: Request photos of the violaceous lesions and wrist for closer inspection.
